(5) Completion of Site Measurement Infrastructure High-speed measurement equipment (PPMS/DDR) was installed and operational at the Wheatridge site, consistent with Task 7. Communication paths, data logging, and configuration settings were validated in preparation for future field disturbances and performance verification. (6) Demonstration Test Plan and Commissioning Frameworks A structured test plan, covering voltage, frequency, and angle-support scenarios, was completed, along with commissioning workflows defining GFM enablement conditions, protection prerequisites, reference alignment steps, and plant-level coordination requirements. 8.2 Significance of These Accomplishments The accomplishments made during BP1 are significant because they: • Establish the technical underpinnings required for safe and effective GFM deployment in large hybrid plants • Provide validated analysis tools supporting weak-grid operation with high inverter penetration • Address industry gaps in both EMT and positive-sequence modeling of GFM behavior • Provide plant-level procedures and measurement infrastructure that reduce commissioning and operational risk • Create a foundation for future field demonstrations and contribute to national understanding of GFM technology readiness Page 23 of 36 Award Number: DE-EE0010651 Recipient Name: Portland General Electric These results accelerate industry-wide capability to study, validate, and ultimately deploy GFM technologies at scale. 8.3 Positive and Negative Outcomes Positive Outcomes: • Completion of all analytical, modeling, risk-assessment, and preparation activities planned for BP1 • Development of simulation, HIL, and commissioning frameworks that did not previously exist for mixed GFM/GFL hybrid plants • Installation of site measurement infrastructure enabling future disturbance validation • Advancement of positive-sequence GFM modeling and hybrid-plant EMT architectures Negative Outcomes: Negative outcomes stem from the early conclusion of BP1, not technical performance: • Field commissioning and demonstration activities could not begin • EMT and HIL models could not be validated against field measurements • Positive-sequence model structures remained at an early development stage • Some planned system-level validation activities remained incomplete 8.4 Milestone Achievement Summary Completed Milestones: • M1.1.1 - Advisory board membership established • M1.1.2 - Consensus on GFM features and performance metrics • M1.2 - Grid-services definitions established • M1.3 - Preliminary validation studies completed • M1.4 - Interconnection study completed • M3.1 - HIL testbed developed • M3.2 - Realistic EMT models completed • M3.4 - Public GFM Type-3 EMT model developed • M7.1 - PPMS installation completed These completed milestones form the technical basis for future tuning, commissioning, and demonstration work. Partially Completed Milestones: • M1.6 - GFM risk assessment (99%) • M2.2 - DDRs and resource-specific studies (21%) • M6.0 - GFM commissioning preparation (8%) Page 24 of 36 Award Number: DE-EE0010651 Recipient Name: Portland General Electric • M8.2 - Positive-sequence GFM Type-3 WTG model (73%) • M8.4 - DC-coupled GFM PV+BESS setup (28%) Partial completions reflect the shortened BP1 period, not performance issues. 8.5 Challenges Encountered The project encountered several technical challenges: (1) Complexity of Mixed GFM/GFL Interactions Coordinating hybrid-plant behavior required careful alignment of inverter-level controls, plant-level supervisors, and EMT assumptions. (2) Sensitivity Under Weak-Grid Conditions Low short-circuit strength introduced heightened sensitivity to inverter-control parameters and required expanded EMT evaluation.
